problems.title: Collect like terms before substitution
problems.question: Evaluate 3(a−4)−4(7−a)−6a at a=17.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: The expression is 3a−12−28+4a−6a=a−40. At 17 it equals −23.

problems.title: Simplify powers by prime factorization
problems.question: Calculate (2⁷·6⁵)/(9³·4⁶).
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: The numerator is 2¹²3⁵ and the denominator 2¹²3⁶. Cancellation leaves 1/3.

problems.title: A linear equation with brackets
problems.question: Solve 4(x−1)−5(2x−7)=x−4.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Expand, then move variable terms to one side.
steps: 4x−4−10x+35=x−4 gives −6x+31=x−4. Therefore 7x=35 and x=5.

problems.title: An isosceles perimeter
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base half as long as either equal side and perimeter 60 cm. Find the base.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: If base is b, equal sides are 2b and 2b.
steps: 5b=60, so b=12 cm. The sides 12,24,24 satisfy the triangle inequality.

problems.title: A perpendicular bisector through a base midpoint
problems.question: AB=BC; D is the midpoint of base AC and lies on the perpendicular bisector of BC. Find the largest angle.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: A perpendicular-bisector point is equidistant from the segment endpoints; the base median of an isosceles triangle is perpendicular to its base.
steps: DB=DC and BD⊥AC. Triangle BDC is therefore right isosceles, with angle DBC=45°.
BD also bisects the apex angle ABC, so ABC=90°, the largest angle.

problems.title: Multiplier for a percentage increase
problems.question: What multiplier increases a positive number by 60%?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: The multiplier is 1.6.

problems.title: Smallest possible class size
problems.question: Four sevenths of a class are girls and 25% of the class play sports. Find the least possible size.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Class size must be divisible by 7 and 4; use their least common multiple.
steps: lcm(7,4)=28. This gives 16 girls and 7 sports participants, both whole numbers.

problems.title: Percent increase in divisor counts
problems.question: By what percent does the number of divisors of 64 exceed the number of divisors of 16?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: 64=2⁶ has 7 positive divisors; 16=2⁴ has 5. The increase is (7−5)/5×100%=40%.

problems.title: Angle between two altitude lines
problems.question: In triangle ABC, C=50°. Find the smaller angle between the altitude lines from A and B.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Rotating both lines by 90° preserves their smaller angle.
steps: The altitude lines are perpendicular to BC and AC. Their smaller angle therefore equals the smaller angle between BC and AC, namely 50°.

problems.title: Angles given as percentages of another
problems.question: A=50% of B and C=30% of B. Find |A−C|.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: 0.5B+B+0.3B=180° gives B=100°, A=50°, C=30°. Their difference is 20°.

problems.title: Minimum sum of two distances
problems.question: Find the minimum of |x+2|+|5−x|.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: Take u=x+2,v=5−x. The sum is at least 7. Equality holds for every −2≤x≤5, so the minimum is 7.

problems.title: A weighted mean fixes a population ratio
problems.question: Athletes average 16 years, coaches 48 years, combined mean 39 years. The total is at most 60. Find the total.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: This gives 9v=23u. Since 9 and 23 are coprime, u=9k,v=23k for a positive integer k.
Total=32k≤60 forces k=1, so there are 32 people.

problems.title: Mix salt solutions by component quantities
problems.question: Mix 10 L of salt:water=2:3 with 20 L of salt:water=3:7. Find the combined ratio.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Component amount = mixture amount times its fraction.
steps: The first contains 4 L-equivalents salt and 6 water. The second contains 6 salt and 14 water.
Together the amounts are 10:20=1:2, using the problem’s additive-mixture model.

problems.title: Perimeter difference after a median cut
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has base 18. A median makes triangles whose perimeters differ by 6. Which listed equal-side length is possible?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: The shared median cancels when perimeters are subtracted.
steps: The median to the base gives equal perimeters, so the median must start at a base vertex and meet an equal side.
If each equal side is s, the perimeter difference is |s+s/2−(18+s/2)|=|s−18|=6. Thus s=12 or 24; both make triangles. Only 12 is listed.
problems.answer: 12 cm among the choices; all possible lengths are 12 and 24 cm.

problems.title: Angle between an altitude and a bisector
problems.question: B=80°,C=60°. Find the angle between the altitude and bisector from A.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: A=40°, so its bisector forms 20° with AB. The altitude forms 90°−80°=10° with AB. Their separation is 20°−10°=10°.

problems.title: Nested absolute values
problems.question: Find the sum of the solutions of ||5x−7|−1|=8.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: |5x−7|−1=8 gives |5x−7|=9. The alternative would give |5x−7|=−7, impossible.
Thus 5x−7=9 or −9, giving x=16/5 or −2/5. Their sum is 14/5=2.8.

problems.title: Combine two ratios
problems.question: First:second=2:3 and second:third=4:7. Their sum is 82. Find largest minus smallest.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Use a common second component: $2:3=8:12$ and $4:7=12:21$.
steps: The combined ratio is 8:12:21, with sum 41 parts. Each part is 2. The numbers are 16,24,42, so the difference is 26.

problems.title: Percent of a sum in a fixed ratio
problems.question: a:b:c=3:4:7 and a+b+c=199199. What percent of a+c is b?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: b/(a+c)=4t/(10t)=2/5=40%. The total is not needed.

problems.title: Clarify which bisector angle is meant
problems.question: The angle between the A and B bisectors is 2.5 times C. Which listed C is possible?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: At the incenter I, $\angle AIB=90°+C/2$; the smaller angle between the two lines is $90°-C/2$.
steps: Using the smaller line angle gives 90°−C/2=2.5C, hence C=30°, a listed choice.
If instead the specified angle means the obtuse angle AIB between the rays toward A and B, 90°+C/2=2.5C gives C=45°, not listed.
problems.answer: 30° under the smaller-angle convention; 45° if angle AIB is intended.
problems.note: The wording does not name the bisector angle. Its interpretation matters; the printed choices support the smaller angle between the lines.

problems.title: Inverse-proportional triangle angles
problems.question: A,B,C are inversely proportional to 2,3,6. Find the smaller angle between A’s bisector line and BC.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: The angles are A=90°,B=60°,C=30°. The A-bisector cuts A into 45° angles.
In triangle ABD, with D on BC, angle ADB=180°−45°−60°=75°. This is the smaller angle of the two lines.

problems.title: Numbers with exactly five divisors
problems.question: How many three-digit positive integers have exactly five positive divisors?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: A divisor count of prime value 5 forces $N=p^4$ for a prime p.
steps: 100≤p⁴≤999 requires 4≤p≤5. The only prime is 5, giving 625.

problems.title: An exact percentage increase must stay integral
problems.question: A factory made 89600 toys in 2021 and plans exactly 25% more each following year. For how many successive years can the condition hold?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: The resulting prime expression is 2^(9−2k)·5^(k+2)·7. It is an integer exactly when 9−2k≥0, so k≤4.
The fifth increase would require half a toy. Four further years are possible.

problems.title: Equivalent equations can both have no solutions
problems.question: Which listed a makes (a−2)(a+3)x=a−3 and |3x−7|=1−a equivalent?
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: Equivalent equations have the same solution set, including the empty set.
steps: At a=2 the first is 0=−1 and has no solution. The second has right side −1 and also has no solution.
At a=−3 only the first is empty; at a=−1 or 0 the second has two roots while the first has one; at a=1 their unique roots differ; at a=3 only the second is empty.

problems.title: Use congruence across intersecting segments
problems.question: AC and BD intersect at E. AB=AE+6, AE=DC,AD=BE and ADC=DEC. Find EC.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
steps: Triangles ADC and BEA have AD=BE,DC=EA and equal included angles, so they are congruent. Consequently AC=BA.
Since E lies on AC, EC=AC−AE=AB−AE=6.

problems.title: Equal perimeters from a trisected median
problems.question: BD is a median, B,M,N,D lie in order with BM=MN=ND. AN=AD and perimeter ABN=12. Find perimeter MDC.
problems.idea: Write the relevant relation, calculate carefully, and check the original restrictions.
formulas: An isosceles triangle has equal base angles; use side-angle-side congruence.
steps: In triangle ADN, AN=AD gives ADN=DNA. Because DC is opposite DA and NB opposite ND, angles CDM and ANB are equal supplements of these equal angles.
DC=AD=AN, and DM=2ND=BN. Thus triangles CDM and ANB are congruent by side-angle-side. Their perimeters are equal.
